newsitem.title: UK: Peregrine reiterates Arvind Mills sell.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine reiterates Arvind Mills sell.

text.p: Peregrine Securities has reiterated its sell recommendation on India's Arvind Mills.
"Arvind's balance sheet and its accounting practices worry us," analyst V Ramanan said in a note to investors.
Peregrine said that the company's non-operating income remains a high proportion of net profit, and that this will continue to remain at levels above 1.0 billion rupees for the next two years.
Also, Arvind's equity investments of 1.3 billion rupees had depreciated by nearly a third of their value and Peregrine estimates the potential investment loss at 425 million rupees.
"The company also has 123.1 million as debtors outstanding for over a year, for which the company has made no provisions," Ramanan said.

Peregrine has revised estimates of Arvind's net profit for fiscal 1997 by 1.3 percent to 1.4 billion rupees and fiscal 1998 by 12.2 percentg to 1.63 billion as a result of the company's capitalisation of two debenture issues.
"However, significant profit downside exists from possible provisions for investment depreciation and outstanding debtors," Peregine said. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
